aria: Animated recap of the Grizzlies' 142 to 111 road win over the Pelicans: Jerami Grant's three with 3:42 left in the second quarter, his second in seven seconds, that made it 62 to 46, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Grant's 22 points off the bench, the top scorers, how the Grizzlies won with 10 players in double figures, and the next game at home against Brooklyn.
notes: Box score from the Grizzlies' 142–111 win over the New Orleans Pelicans at the Smoothie King Center on Nov 13, 2026, an NBA Cup group game, from the StatMuse box score and play log, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News and Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker and Sports Capitol DC), The Commercial Appeal (via Yahoo Sports), Grizzlies on SI, Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker) and Crescent City Sports. All 142 Memphis points and all 111 New Orleans points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 70–58 Memphis at the half and 105–86 after three (StatMuse; Fox Sports; AP). Biggest leads: Memphis 31, New Orleans 3 (StatMuse). Bench points (76–27) are from The Commercial Appeal; the other team stats are StatMuse's. Records and ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Friday's games.

Memphis matched an NBA record with 10 players in double figures, a franchise record (AP; The Commercial Appeal): Jerami Grant 22, Ty Jerome 17, Cedric Coward 14, Cam Spencer 14, GG Jackson 14, Cam Boozer 12, Isaiah Stewart 12, Jaylen Wells 11, Taylor Hendricks 10 and Javon Small 10. Grant's 22 off the bench is a season high (Field Level Media). Memphis is 6–0 on the road (Field Level Media); New Orleans has lost five straight (Field Level Media) and won the Nov 2 meeting 135–134 in overtime (site scores). Memphis hosts Brooklyn on Saturday at 8:00 PM ET (site schedule).

How it broke open: Memphis scored 13 straight in the second quarter, from 49–46 to 62–46 (AP; StatMuse play log). New Orleans got within 80–77 on a Saddiq Bey three with 6:01 left in the third; Memphis answered with a 25–9 run to lead 105–86 after three (Yahoo Sports; StatMuse play log).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Grant's 24-foot three with 3:42 left in the second quarter, which made it 62–46. Seven seconds earlier he had made a 27-foot three and a free throw for an illegal closeout by Zion Williamson (AP: "Grant had seven points in seven seconds, nailing a pair of 3s and adding a foul shot"; StatMuse play log, 3:49 and 3:42). The shot is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Memphis Grizzlies or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Grant's listed 6-foot-7 and 210 pounds, with arms scaled to his 7-foot-2.75 wingspan measured at the 2014 draft combine (CraftedNBA; Tankathon), in Memphis's road blue with No. 3 (AP photo caption). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
